Calculator Guide

Calculator Guide

Exact button order for common field calculations. Enter the number before its unit or construction key.

Basic arithmeticEnter the first value, press +, −, ×, or ÷, enter the second value, then press =.Example: 25 × 4 = → 100
Feet, inches, and fractionsEnter feet, press Feet, enter inches, press Inch, then enter the numerator, /, and denominator.Example: 5 Feet 4 Inch 15 / 16 → 5 ft 4 15/16 in
Mixed measurement mathMeasurements may be added, subtracted, multiplied by a number, or divided by a number. ARCcalc keeps the dimensional unit.Example: 5 ft 4 in + 2 ft 8 in = → 8 ft 0 in
Unit conversionEnter a measurement, press Conv, then press the destination unit. Compatible units convert directly.Example: 36 Inch Conv Feet → 3 ft
Right triangleStore any two values with Rise, Run, or Diag, then press the missing key to solve it.Example: 3 Feet Rise, 4 Feet Run, Diag → 5 ft
Pitch layoutStore pitch and run, then solve rise or diagonal. Pitch is entered as inches of rise per 12 inches of run.Example: 7 Pitch, 12 Feet Run, Rise → 7 ft
Stair calculationEnter total rise and press Rise. Optionally enter total run and press Run. Press Stair, then continue pressing Stair or use ▲/▼ to review each result.Results include riser height, riser count, over/under, tread width, tread count, stringer length, and angle.
Circle calculationEnter the diameter and press Circ. Continue pressing Circ or use ▲/▼ to cycle diameter, area in square feet, area in square inches, and circumference.
Square and square rootPress Conv then Sqr to square a value. Press Sqr by itself for square root. Length squared becomes area, and area square root becomes length.
PercentPress % to divide the displayed value by 100 while preserving its compatible unit.Example: 25 % → 0.25
Alternate functionsPress Conv before another key to use its alternate function. Useful shortcuts include Conv + 7 for desired riser, Conv + 9 for desired tread, Conv + 5 for jack spacing, and Conv + 0 for material density.
Editing and clearingBack removes the latest entry. Clear clears the current calculation. Invalid dimensions, zero denominators, and division by zero display an error instead of a result.

Welding Parameters

INPUT

Enter the observed values from the machine, WPS, or inspection record.

Formula and efficiency help

Heat input = voltage × amperage × 60 ÷ travel speed ÷ 1000 × efficiency. Use the efficiency required by the applicable procedure, code, or project specification.

02

Travel Speed (IPM)

INPUT

Select weld time and completed length to calculate inches per minute.

—
Choose time and length, then calculate.
How travel speed is measured

IPM = weld length in inches × 60 ÷ elapsed seconds. Example: 6 inches in 30 seconds equals 12 IPM.
